children: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has issued an executive order declaring a statewide disaster emergency over the ongoing measles outbreak, with more than 100 cases reported in the state.

The executive order extends the pool of health professionals who can administer measles vaccines to include paramedics, advanced EMS providers, pharmacists and midwives. It also allows nurses to order testing.
"No one should get seriously ill or die from a vaccine-preventable disease," Hochul said. "That is why I have taken steps to increase the number of health professionals who can vaccinate and test."
As of Oct. 3, there have been seven confirmed cases in New York City and 101 in New York State outside of NYC.

The state government called on New Yorkers to ensure they are up-to-date on their measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccines. All MMR vaccinations must be reported to state or NYC immunization registries within 72 hours of administration.
Neighboring Pennsylvania has surpassed 1,000 measles cases and reported five measles-associated deaths this year. That makes it the largest state outbreak in over three decades.
As of Oct. 1, 3,887 confirmed measles cases were reported in the U.S. this year, up from 2,289 in 2025.
MMR vaccines are manufactured primarily by Merck
